messages:
morgan: Hey folks — pinging runtime/platform/infra/security for a quick merge-gate check on PR #15499. Adds a new runtime fallback policy that routes to a 4-bit quantized variant under high load. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/15499. Need approvals: runtime (latency/regressions), infra (routing/fallback infra), security (KMS/secret surface). Targeting a short canary tomorrow AM. TL;DR: new config flag + small runtime router change + policy rule.

sam: Quick skim — looks small. What's the expected perf delta for p99 when fallback kicks in?

morgan: Good q. Measured locally on A100: p99 increases ~30ms for short sequences when falling back to the quantized variant, but end-to-end throughput and tail cost under saturation both improve. I added the bench numbers to the PR description and a short table.

cheng: Two asks: 1) add an integration test that simulates the capacity fallback (left a comment in the tests folder), and 2) gate behind a feature flag so we can toggle during canary.

yuki: Security quick note: I checked the diff — no new secrets or KMS calls introduced. Only changed routing logic and a config toggle. Can we include a short note in the changelog about the behavior change?

devsec-bot: CI status — checks/ci-pipeline passed, checks/e2e failed on test 'route_retries_test' (flaky). Rerun recommended.

morgan: Thanks. Pushed an extra test per cheng and added `fallback.enable_by_default=false` so canary opts in. Triggered CI rerun.

sam: +1 from runtime for the code changes and perf notes (will monitor tail latency during canary).

cheng: I'll take infra. One question: does the fallback require updating any long-lived routing table or eviction headers? If so we need a migration step for older proxies.

morgan: It doesn't mutate persisted routing tables — decision is made at request time using the policy engine. I added a comment in runtime/router.go explaining that. No migration needed.

cheng: OK, infra +1 on approach but I'll hold final operational +1 until we verify canary metrics (eviction rate, retries).

yuki: Security +1, no secrets changed. Please add a one-line changelog entry about privacy/telemetry implications.

morgan: Added the changelog line and a short note in the PR about what metrics to watch.

sam: Formal runtime approval +1. Morgan — please schedule canary and ping SRE.

morgan: Canary scheduled for 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC for 2 hours. I'll post the canary dashboard link in #eng-sre and will roll back if errors spike.

devsec-bot: Merge queue — all checks green after rerun. Auto-merge eligible.

morgan: Merged and cut release candidate. Thanks everyone :tada:
